title: I'm hoping for my happy ending, says cancer survivor mum

evidence_packet.title: I'm hoping for my happy ending, says cancer survivor mum
evidence_packet.lead: A Manchester mum living with stage four cancer celebrates after recent scans showed no signs of cancer
evidence_packet.summary: A Manchester mum living with stage four cancer celebrates after recent scans showed no signs of cancer
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A mum re-diagnosed with cancer while 35 weeks pregnant said she was now hoping she could "finally have my happy ending" Annie Fields, 37, from Manchester, was first diagnosed with breast cancer in 2021 She was eventually given the all clear and looking forward to being a mother when she received in 2024 the devastating news that her cancer had returned and was at stage four She had an early emergency caesarean to deliver her son, now two, and surgery to remove a brain tumour After treatment and pioneering immunotherapy she went into remission but was again re-diagnosed with cancer last year After more surgery and treatment she is now celebrating an unexpected "miracle" clear full-body scan

title: Disabled mum backs campaign for better paternity leave

evidence_packet.title: Disabled mum backs campaign for better paternity leave
evidence_packet.lead: Melissa Johns, 36, from Greater Manchester, says two weeks paternity leave is 'not enough' in 2026
evidence_packet.summary: Melissa Johns, 36, from Greater Manchester, says two weeks paternity leave is 'not enough' in 2026
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A disabled mum from Greater Manchester has joined a campaign for better paternity leave after being "stopped in her tracks" by the challenges of adapting to motherhood alone Melissa Johns, 36, from Ashton-under-Lyne, welcomed her first child in October Despite requiring six weeks to recover from a caesarean section, Melissa - who was born without a fully formed right arm - was left to face maternity leave alone after her partner went back to work when their daughter was two weeks old She has now joined a campaign to change the law to let fathers take longer paternity leave, and to receive a bigger proportion of their salary when they do But sceptics say such changes would have a significant impact on businesses, and question how they could be afforded Melissa said: "Having one arm means that I rely on my core strength a lot more," Melissa said

title: Ex-boxer Frank Bruno supports scheme to deliver free footballs

evidence_packet.title: Ex-boxer Frank Bruno supports scheme to deliver free footballs
evidence_packet.lead: Non-profit initiative Found Football leaves footballs in parks to encourage children to exercise
evidence_packet.summary: Non-profit initiative Found Football leaves footballs in parks to encourage children to exercise
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Former boxing world champion Frank Bruno has distributed free footballs to local parks in support of a scheme encouraging children to get active The 64-year-old delivered 10 footballs to Southchurch Park in Southend-on-Sea and the nearby village of Hockley in Essex Ritchie Beckett, the director of non-profit initiative Found Football, is pledging to drop more of them in the county's parks before the end of the year The 44-year-old dad from Stockport said Bruno's support took the movement "to another level" and he wanted it to go "nationwide" in the future On social media, Bruno said he hoped it would prevent children from getting involved with "other activities" "If a small game of football between a few people means they won't be up to other things in the park it gets my thumbs up," said the former WBC heavyweight champion

title: Convicted murderer recorded himself planning to kidnap a teenager

evidence_packet.title: Convicted murderer recorded himself planning to kidnap a teenager
evidence_packet.lead: Paul Sharpe, from Stockport, was sentenced to a life with a minimum term of eight years
evidence_packet.summary: Paul Sharpe, from Stockport, was sentenced to a life with a minimum term of eight years
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A convicted murderer has received a second life jail term for the knifepoint kidnap in broad daylight of a 15-year-old girl who he went on to sexually assault Paul Sharpe, 56, bundled his teenage victim into a car in Altrincham, Greater Manchester, on 18 May Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court heard Sharpe - jailed in 2001 for murdering an ex-partner - had been to the area months before and had recorded voice memos detailing his planned "abduction point" Sharpe, from Portswood, Stockport, was ordered to serve a minimum of eight years in jail before he can be considered for release by the Parole Board The court heard the teenager was kept captive in Sharpe's car for eight and a half hours before she was rescued by police the following day In fear that she was going to be raped and murdered, she showed "an astonishing presence of mind" to tear out strands of hair to provide DNA proof she had been in the vehicle, the court was told

title: Union calls for new university leadership after boss sacked

evidence_packet.title: Union calls for new university leadership after boss sacked
evidence_packet.lead: Unison members at the University of Greater Manchester are calling for governors to step aside
evidence_packet.summary: Unison members at the University of Greater Manchester are calling for governors to step aside
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trade union members at the University of Greater Manchester have staged a protest demanding "greater transparency" following the sacking of the former vice chancellor professor George Holmes Unison members at the institution in Bolton said the current board of governors should step aside, arguing the university can only move on with a "clean slate" Holmes was suspended after the university commissioned an independent inquiry into allegations of financial mismanagement and other misconduct A university spokesperson said it "took the time to talk to staff members and listen to concerns raised" at the protest Unison representative Paul Chanin, said: "The current board of governors, who were around when George Holmes was around, need to look at themselves, to understand whether they should be remaining in post." Holmes had been in post for 20 years before he was suspended following an independent inquiry into allegations raised in an investigation by The Mill , external in 2025

title: Jury sworn in for trial of husband accused of drugging and raping wife with 12 others

evidence_packet.title: Jury sworn in for trial of husband accused of drugging and raping wife with 12 others
evidence_packet.lead: Prosecutors allege the Stockport woman was abused for more than 20 years without her knowledge
evidence_packet.summary: Prosecutors allege the Stockport woman was abused for more than 20 years without her knowledge
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A jury has been sworn in for the trial of a man accused of drugging and raping his wife for almost 20 years before allegedly inviting other men to join the abuse The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, has already admitted 15 charges including rape However he denies 33 other counts and will stand trial alongside 12 other men at Minshull Street Crown Court in Manchester Prosecutors allege the men sexually abused the victim at her home in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester, while she was drugged and completely unaware of what was happening A 14th defendant, 59-year-old Keith Fotheringham from Dundee, Scotland, has pleaded guilty to all four charges he faced including conspiracy to rape, conspiracy to assault by penetration, conspiracy to administer a substance with intent and assault by penetration The husband's alleged offending dates back to 2004 while the other men are accused of joining in the abuse between September 2018 until November 2025 - when the arrests were made

title: Bolton man skipping length of UK to 'spread joy and kindness'

evidence_packet.title: Bolton man skipping length of UK to 'spread joy and kindness'
evidence_packet.lead: Krish Patel is doing the equivalent of 40 marathons in 40 days for a charity challenge
evidence_packet.summary: Krish Patel is doing the equivalent of 40 marathons in 40 days for a charity challenge
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man has pledged to skip the length of the UK on a mission to "prove kindness exists everywhere" Krish Patel is skipping 900 miles (1148 km) from Land's End to John O'Groats - the equivalent of 40 marathons in 40 days - during his Great British Skip challenge The 34-year-old, from Bolton, Greater Manchester, said he was inspired after seeing skipping children "laughing with joy" while he was volunteering at schools in Uganda and Manchester "It clearly brings smiles, it brings joy so I thought, you know what, what about if I skip the length of the UK with a skipping rope," he told BBC Radio Manchester He began the challenge on 18 August and expects to finish in Scotland on 26 September and hopes to raise £520,000 for charity "I wondered if anyone had ever done it before," Patel said

title: Man City stadium lease reviewed amid Etihad Campus expansion

evidence_packet.title: Man City stadium lease reviewed amid Etihad Campus expansion
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester City has a long-term lease with the city council for the ground in the east of the city
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester City has a long-term lease with the city council for the ground in the east of the city
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City's lease at the Etihad Stadium was placed under review last month amid a major expansion of the club's east Manchester campus, it has emerged City has a long-term lease at the ground with Manchester City Council and finished expanding its north stand earlier this year, which increased the stadium capacity to more than 60,000 people It has been building a new £300m entertainment zone known as Medlock Square which includes a Radisson Blu Hotel and a zip-line, with plans for a new 600-person capacity entertainment venue which the council granted planning permission in June The lease review was sparked as a result of changes taking place around the Etihad Campus, the Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS) understands Council papers describing a decision about a "variation of leases with Manchester City Football Club" have been made public on the town hall's website but specifics of the finances have been kept hidden from view The review is expected to result in an uplift in the yearly base rate fee paid to the city council from the club, currently said to be between £3m to £4m a year

evidence_packet.title: The night Madonna performed at the Haçienda for £50, then wiped it from her memory
evidence_packet.lead: “I think she's a wonderful artist and I love the way she's so rude to people,” the late Tony Wilson once said of Madonna.

And he should know The Factory Records boss had first-hand experience with the pop superstar’s brusque manner after she performed at the Haçienda in 1984 for
evidence_packet.evidence_text: “I think she's a wonderful artist and I love the way she's so rude to people,” the late Tony Wilson once said of Madonna. And he should know The Factory Records boss had first-hand experience with the pop superstar’s brusque manner after she performed at the Haçienda in 1984 for the princely sum of £50 The bargain price gig was negotiated by television executive Malcolm Gerrie, who persuaded Madonna's record company to organise her appearance at the venue as part of a one-off, live Channel 4 broadcast of cult music show The Tube View 4 Images Madonna performing at The Hacienda, Manchester, on an episode of The Tube (Image: Channel 4/The Tube/YouTube screengrab) Free ticket-holders to the Haçienda showcase on January 27, 1984 were there to see the Factory Allstars - a band pulled together for the night by members of Durutti Column, A Certain Ratio, Quando Quango and soul singer Marcel King. So they were bemused when Madonna rocked up on Flanked by two Lycra-clad backing dancers, the then 25-year-old spun and gyrated as she sang Holiday. Her brother Christopher Ciccone - who was a backing dancer at the Haçienda gig - recounted their time in Manchester in his book, Life With My Sister

It opened for traffic from January 1, 1894. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Stockport murderer who kidnapped girl off street and sexually attacked her in horror eight-hour ordeal jailed for life Paul Sharpe held his victim hostage for eight hours before they were found by police in a hotel car park News Stephen Topping A convicted murderer who kidnapped a girl at knifepoint before sexually assaulting her has been jailed for life. Paul Sharpe held his 15-year-old victim hostage during a grim eight-hour ordeal, as he drove from one car park to another The 56-year-old put the girl in a headlock and bundled her into his car on Bradgate Road, in Altrincham , at around 7.30pm on May 18 - claiming that her father owed him money. He drove to a car park at Manchester Airport and tied up her ankles and wrists with a neck tie That night, he drove to different car parks in Greater Manchester and Cheshire, and plied the girl with alcohol while sexually assaulting her. At one point, former radio DJ Sharpe masturbated while touching the girl's feet, the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said He was finally caught by police in a hotel car park in Knutsford at around 3.40am on May 19. The girl had been reported as missing by her mother, while CCTV allowed officers to identify Sharpe's car, according to the CPS Greater Manchester Police says the girl had been studying at Sale Library on May 18 before beginning her journey home with friends at around 5:50pm. At 6:10pm, she contacted her parents to let them know she was on her way home

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Jury sworn in at trial of Stockport husband accused of drugging and raping wife with 12 co-defendants The husband, a man in his 60s from Stockport, denies 33 charges News Andrew Bardsley and Amy Walker Court reporter 12:37, 04 Sep 2026 View 4 I A jury has been sworn in at the trial of 12 men accused of sexual offences after a husband allegedly drugged and raped his wife over a number of years The husband, a man in his 60s from Stockport, denies 33 charges, including conspiracy to rape, conspiracy to commit assault by penetration, conspiracy to administer a substance with intent, rape and sexual assault. The charges relate to a 20 year period The Manchester Evening News and other media organisations are not naming the man in order to protect the anonymity of his alleged victim. They are Karl Lindsay, Daniel Rayner, Graham Brougham, Philip Wild, Mohammed Sabir, Jonathan Kirk, Sean Peers, Jordan Wallace, Alan Keelan, Richard Townsend, Robert Stewart and David Graves. All charges relate to the same sin A jury of 12 people, nine women and three men, were sworn in at Minshull Street Crown Court on Friday (September 4). evidence_packet.evidence_text: M67 Police issue major update one month after human remains discovered next to M67 Officers have made a breakthrough News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 12:27, 04 Sep 2026 View Image Police and forensics officers on the M67 after the discovery of hum Police have issued a major investigation update a month after human remains were found next to the M67 motorway. Road workers made the tragic discovery near a bridge between junctions three at Hyde and four at Hattersley on Monday. August 3 The motorway remained closed eastbound the following day as officers and forensics investigators carried out enquiries. Greater Manchester Police later confirmed that the remains were believed to belong to a man aged between 20 and 28 He was thought to have been between 5ft 5ins and 5ft 9ins tall, and of medium build. In a further update issued today (September 4), GMP says it has since identified the person's next of kin Officers are continuing to establish the circumstances of how the man ended up where he did and what caused his death. Details on when the man may have died are yet to be confirmed The discovery was made by road workers during routine maintenance on the M67, in Tameside . A Home Office post-mortem later took place as officers tried to piece together the clues of what happened to the man. Enquiries remain ongoing

title: The night Madonna performed at the Haçienda for £50, then wiped it from her memory

evidence_packet.title: The night Madonna performed at the Haçienda for £50, then wiped it from her memory
evidence_packet.lead: “I think she's a wonderful artist and I love the way she's so rude to people,” the late Tony Wilson once said of Madonna.
evidence_packet.summary: “I think she's a wonderful artist and I love the way she's so rude to people,” the late Tony Wilson once said of Madonna. And he should know The Factory Records boss had first-hand experience with the pop superstar’s brusque manner after she performed at the Haçienda in 1984 for
evidence_packet.evidence_text: “I think she's a wonderful artist and I love the way she's so rude to people,” the late Tony Wilson once said of Madonna. And he should know The Factory Records boss had first-hand experience with the pop superstar’s brusque manner after she performed at the Haçienda in 1984 for the princely sum of £50 The bargain price gig was negotiated by television executive Malcolm Gerrie, who persuaded Madonna's record company to organise her appearance at the venue as part of a one-off, live Channel 4 broadcast of cult music show The Tube View 4 Images Madonna performing at The Hacienda, Manchester, on an episode of The Tube (Image: Channel 4/The Tube/YouTube screengrab) Free ticket-holders to the Haçienda showcase on January 27, 1984 were there to see the Factory Allstars - a band pulled together for the night by members of Durutti Column, A Certain Ratio, Quando Quango and soul singer Marcel King. So they were bemused when Madonna rocked up on Flanked by two Lycra-clad backing dancers, the then 25-year-old spun and gyrated as she sang Holiday. Her brother Christopher Ciccone - who was a backing dancer at the Haçienda gig - recounted their time in Manchester in his book, Life With My Sister

evidence_packet.lead: NHS Bullying and safety fears at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust as hundreds of staff report issues The concerns were shared in a report View 3 Images MFT runs hospitals across the city, employing more than 30,000 members of staff Comments News Declan Carey Local Democ
evidence_packet.summary: NHS Bullying and safety fears at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust as hundreds of staff report issues The concerns were shared in a report View 3 Images MFT runs hospitals across the city, employing more than 30,000 members of staff Comments News Declan Carey Local Democ
evidence_packet.evidence_text: NHS Bullying and safety fears at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust as hundreds of staff report issues The concerns were shared in a report View 3 Images MFT runs hospitals across the city, employing more than 30,000 members of staff Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 07:23, 05 Sep 2026 Updated 07:23, 05 Sep 2026 Hundreds of hospital workers in Manchester have reported experiences of safety fears as well as bullying and harassment at work, according to a report from the country’s largest NHS Workers at the Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) reported more than 380 incidents in total over the past year, up from 204 incidents in 2023-24. Staff concerns reported included ‘bullying behaviours by people in positions of authority’ and ‘harassment linked to pro Many reported experiencing issues with ‘unprofessional behaviour’ and ‘leadership approaches leaving colleagues feeling undervalued, anxious or unsafe at work’ They also raised concerns over intense workload pressures, such as staffing gaps and rota changes putting staff at risk of ‘burnout’ while working in Manchester’s healthcare facilities MFT runs hospitals across the city including North Manchester General Hospital, Manchester Royal Infirmary, and Trafford General, employing more than 30,000 members of staff in total

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Christie Hospital She though she was tired from university, then she woke up Claudia Boardman feared she was going to die after being diagnosed with an extremely rare and aggressive form of cancer Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovati Claudia Boardman was only 20 when she first began experiencing a strange, persistent feeling in her back. At the time, she was studying to become a midwife Initially, Claire, from Nantwich, Cheshire, put the pain down to the demands of university and working on a delivery suite. She was wrong Months later, she woke up unable to feel her legs. There was no feeling, and from her chest down and felt "numb and tingly" DONATE TO THE FUNDRAISER BY THE CHRISTIE CHARITY AND MANCHESTER EVENING NEWS HERE The student medic was rushed to A&E. There, a scan revealed a lesion in her back, and doctors later discovered it was a tumour wrapped around her spine and pressing on her spinal cord

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Christie Hospital Manchester Evening News launches £42.5m campaign to revolutionise cancer care at The Christie The Manchester Evening News is launching a joint fundraiser to expand capacity at the world-renowned hospital News Bethan Finighan Scie We want to raise £42.5m to construct a groundbreaking new scanning centre at the world-renowned hospital as demand for vital diagnostic imaging triples. The existing unit was built nearly 50 years ago to cater for around 20 patients a day Now, it supports more than 60, with demand continuing to rise as cancer diagnoses increase The Manchester Evening News is backing The Christie Charity’s £42.5m appeal. Every donation will help pave the way for the new scanning centre closer and give thousands of cancer patients access to faster and more advanced imaging DONATE TO THE SCANNING CENTRE FUNDRAISER HERE Every patient at The Christie will visit the scanning centre at some point - as part of diagnosis, during treatment or throughout ongoing follow-up care

evidence_packet.title: 'They both begin with 'B' and that's where it ends': Six miles apart, life in these Stockport neighbourhoods is very different
evidence_packet.lead: Stockport 'They both begin with 'B' and that's where it ends': Six miles apart, life in these Stockport neighbourhoods is very different They share a borough, but there's a clear divide - in finances, amenities and, as new data makes painfully clear, Comments News David Dubas-Fis
evidence_packet.summary: Stockport 'They both begin with 'B' and that's where it ends': Six miles apart, life in these Stockport neighbourhoods is very different They share a borough, but there's a clear divide - in finances, amenities and, as new data makes painfully clear, Comments News David Dubas-Fis
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport 'They both begin with 'B' and that's where it ends': Six miles apart, life in these Stockport neighbourhoods is very different They share a borough, but there's a clear divide - in finances, amenities and, as new data makes painfully clear, Comments News David Dubas-Fisher Data Investigations Editor and Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 07:13, 05 Sep 2026 On a mild Friday afternoon, a handful of people are milling about the precinct in Brinnington, a suburb of Stockport nestled beside the M60 Just under six miles away, parking spaces are hard to come by in the leafy village of Bramhall . The difference is clear - one an area where people feel left behind, the other a place people aspire to call home The lives of Stopfordians in Brinnington and Bramhall are very different. They share a borough, but there's a clear divide - in finances, amenities and, as new data makes painfully clear, life expectancy According to the latest figures from the Office for National Statistics (ONS), men in Brinnington have an average healthy life expectancy of 50.5 years. That's the lowest in the Greater Manchester For men in Bramhall West, it's 75.3 years. That's the highest in Greater Manchester and one one of the highest in the country

title: Blood, sweat, tears and Manchester United: The story of the Irish in Trafford

evidence_packet.title: Blood, sweat, tears and Manchester United: The story of the Irish in Trafford
evidence_packet.lead: Premium Blood, sweat, tears and Manchester United: The story of the Irish in Trafford An exhibition of Irish history and culture in the borough is being planned View 5 Images Navvies working on the Manchester Ship Canal which took six years to build Comments News Neal Keeling Chi
evidence_packet.summary: Premium Blood, sweat, tears and Manchester United: The story of the Irish in Trafford An exhibition of Irish history and culture in the borough is being planned View 5 Images Navvies working on the Manchester Ship Canal which took six years to build Comments News Neal Keeling Chi
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Premium Blood, sweat, tears and Manchester United: The story of the Irish in Trafford An exhibition of Irish history and culture in the borough is being planned View 5 Images Navvies working on the Manchester Ship Canal which took six years to build Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 07:12, 05 Sep 2026 It was a link forged with blood sweat and tears. It was later bolstered by Gaelic talent gracing the home of The Red Devils The Irish connection to the borough of Trafford is woven deep through the history of its industry and sporting legends In this corner of Greater Manchester, navvies toiled over six years to create the foundation of a magnificent feat of engineering - the Manchester Ship Canal. It opened for traffic from January 1, 1894. It cost more than £15m, equivalent today to £2.1bn Queen Victoria officially opened the canal on May 21, 1894 An estimated 17,000 workers grafted to make the 36 miles waterway from Salford to the Irish Sea. Workers came from Ireland - around 5,000 of them. The others came from Scotland, Wales, and South West England as well as the streets of Manchester and Salford

title: Police probe vile hoax TikTok knife threats as bag checks carried out at Salford school

evidence_packet.title: Police probe vile hoax TikTok knife threats as bag checks carried out at Salford school
evidence_packet.lead: Salford Police probe vile hoax TikTok knife threats as bag checks carried out at Salford school The Manchester Evening News understands there is no link between an knife attack in Walkden and a suspected hoax at Co-op Academy Walkden News Chris Slater Images seen by the Mancheste
evidence_packet.summary: Salford Police probe vile hoax TikTok knife threats as bag checks carried out at Salford school The Manchester Evening News understands there is no link between an knife attack in Walkden and a suspected hoax at Co-op Academy Walkden News Chris Slater Images seen by the Mancheste
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Police probe vile hoax TikTok knife threats as bag checks carried out at Salford school The Manchester Evening News understands there is no link between an knife attack in Walkden and a suspected hoax at Co-op Academy Walkden News Chris Slater Images seen by the Manchester Evening News were circulated on a social media platform, understood to be TikTok, on Thursday evening (September 3). One showed a hand holding a bladed weapon while another showed an image of armed police The picture of the knife carried the caption: 'Coop Walkden I'm After You Next.' After officers were called in over the disturbing content on the social media site, the MEN was contacted by a number of concerned parents of children at Co-op Academy Walkden in Salford The school acted quickly with security being stepped up including increased monitoring of access. Bag checks were also carried out, with nothing untoward being found following the purported threats, which are being treated as a hoax A second image shared on the social media platform featured a picture of an armed police officer and the words 'them tomorrow at coop academy walkden.'

It's a scene of joy to watch the young and old play together View 6 Images The award-winnin
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Three-year-old Nico wanders over to 96-year-old June with a bag filled with toys, and she rummages around to produce a rubber duckie to his beaming delight and squeals from the other kids. It's a scene of joy to watch the young and old play together View 6 Images The award-winning Fernlea Care Home, which has a children’s nursery, Fernbee’s on site (Image: Manchester Evening News) This is a care home with a difference. It’s home to residents, currently up to 106 years of age. But also on the site is the Fernbees nursery, with youngsters aged from just six months, who regularly pop in for a tea break or lunch The two communities happily mix in an inter-generational model that has won praise from both its care users and the wider industry. Our Lifestyle Editor Dianne Bourne popped down for a visit and brought us this joyful despatch After the sing song in the main lounge, Dianne watched as the kids and older residents moved over to the bar area to tuck in to some tea, squash and cakes and have a chit chat. She describes the lovely image of June - a former Stockport mayor - playing games with the younger kids “The kids behave beautifully, they really do. I did wonder at first but they’re just lovely."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Mancunian Way ‘I hope one day there won’t be a need for Pride - we’re certainly not there yet’ As Manchester Pride ushers in a new dawn, a new Mancunian Way podcast looks at where it went wrong and what the future looks like for this vital event. “I hope one day - and I don't know whether it will be in my lifetime or not - there won't be a need for Pride because everyone will be equal,” says Steph Kay. “We're certainly not there yet.” It started with a few trestle tables and some games to raise money for AIDS sufferers. It transformed into a behemoth with international stars to rival the world’s biggest festivals View 4 Images All the thrills of the Manchester Gay Pub and Club Olympics in 1985 As a long-standing Gay Village businesswoman, Steph has seen Manchester Pride take many forms. The former manager of lesbian bar Vanilla has worked and partied throughout the event over decades. She was, at one time, a trustee of the event But Steph says the festival ‘snowballed’ after she left, with organisers deciding to hire bigger artists and venues. It was these decisions that culminated in the controversial choice to move Pride out of the Village entirely

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Stockport murderer who kidnapped girl off street and sexually attacked her in horror eight-hour ordeal jailed for life Paul Sharpe held his victim hostage for eight hours before they were found by police in a hotel car park News Stephen Topping A convicted murderer who kidnapped a girl at knifepoint before sexually assaulting her has been jailed for life. Paul Sharpe held his 15-year-old victim hostage during a grim eight-hour ordeal, as he drove from one car park to another The 56-year-old put the girl in a headlock and bundled her into his car on Bradgate Road, in Altrincham , at around 7.30pm on May 18 - claiming that her father owed him money. He drove to a car park at Manchester Airport and tied up her ankles and wrists with a neck tie That night, he drove to different car parks in Greater Manchester and Cheshire, and plied the girl with alcohol while sexually assaulting her. At one point, former radio DJ Sharpe masturbated while touching the girl's feet, the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said He was finally caught by police in a hotel car park in Knutsford at around 3.40am on May 19. The girl had been reported as missing by her mother, while CCTV allowed officers to identify Sharpe's car, according to the CPS Greater Manchester Police says the girl had been studying at Sale Library on May 18 before beginning her journey home with friends at around 5:50pm. At 6:10pm, she contacted her parents to let them know she was on her way home

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Jury sworn in at trial of Stockport husband accused of drugging and raping wife with 12 co-defendants The husband, a man in his 60s from Stockport, denies 33 charges News Andrew Bardsley and Amy Walker Court reporter 12:37, 04 Sep 2026 View 4 I A jury has been sworn in at the trial of 12 men accused of sexual offences after a husband allegedly drugged and raped his wife over a number of years The husband, a man in his 60s from Stockport, denies 33 charges, including conspiracy to rape, conspiracy to commit assault by penetration, conspiracy to administer a substance with intent, rape and sexual assault. The charges relate to a 20 year period The Manchester Evening News and other media organisations are not naming the man in order to protect the anonymity of his alleged victim. The law entitles the alleged victim to anonymity for life The other 12 defendants deny the charges against them. They are Karl Lindsay, Daniel Rayner, Graham Brougham, Philip Wild, Mohammed Sabir, Jonathan Kirk, Sean Peers, Jordan Wallace, Alan Keelan, Richard Townsend, Robert Stewart and David Graves. All charges relate to the same sin A jury of 12 people, nine women and three men, were sworn in at Minshull Street Crown Court on Friday (September 4). They were sent away until Wednesday morning (September 9). Two alternative jurors, two women, were also selected

evidence_packet.evidence_text: M67 Police issue major update one month after human remains discovered next to M67 Officers have made a breakthrough News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 12:27, 04 Sep 2026 View Image Police and forensics officers on the M67 after the discovery of hum Police have issued a major investigation update a month after human remains were found next to the M67 motorway. Road workers made the tragic discovery near a bridge between junctions three at Hyde and four at Hattersley on Monday. August 3 The motorway remained closed eastbound the following day as officers and forensics investigators carried out enquiries. Greater Manchester Police later confirmed that the remains were believed to belong to a man aged between 20 and 28 He was thought to have been between 5ft 5ins and 5ft 9ins tall, and of medium build. In a further update issued today (September 4), GMP says it has since identified the person's next of kin Officers are continuing to establish the circumstances of how the man ended up where he did and what caused his death. Details on when the man may have died are yet to be confirmed The discovery was made by road workers during routine maintenance on the M67, in Tameside . A Home Office post-mortem later took place as officers tried to piece together the clues of what happened to the man. Enquiries remain ongoing

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Whalley Range Police descend on Whalley Range street at 1am with two arrested after driver smashes into parked car Officers seized drugs from the scene in Whalley Range, Manchester News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 12:18, 04 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Two people have been arrested after a driver ploughed into a parked car in south Manchester. Officers were called out to Alexandra Road, in Whalley Range , at around 1am this morning (September 4) Greater Manchester Police says a 25-year-old man was arrested at the scene on suspicion of drink driving. Officers went on to conduct a search, before seizing quantities of suspected Class A, B and C drugs The driver and his passenger, a 17-year-old boy, were subsequently arrested on suspicion of possession with intent to supply controlled drugs. The stationary vehicle was unoccupied at the time of the crash and no injuries were reported, GMP says Both suspects remain in custody for questioning this morning (Friday). evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Christie Hospital She though she was tired from university, then she woke up Claudia Boardman feared she was going to die after being diagnosed with an extremely rare and aggressive form of cancer Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovati Claudia Boardman was only 20 when she first began experiencing a strange, persistent feeling in her back. At the time, she was studying to become a midwife Initially, Claire, from Nantwich, Cheshire, put the pain down to the demands of university and working on a delivery suite. She was wrong Months later, she woke up unable to feel her legs. There was no feeling, and from her chest down and felt "numb and tingly" DONATE TO THE FUNDRAISER BY THE CHRISTIE CHARITY AND MANCHESTER EVENING NEWS HERE The student medic was rushed to A&E. There, a scan revealed a lesion in her back, and doctors later discovered it was a tumour wrapped around her spine and pressing on her spinal cord

title: The night Madonna performed at the Haçienda for £50, then wiped it from her memory

evidence_packet.title: The night Madonna performed at the Haçienda for £50, then wiped it from her memory
evidence_packet.lead: “I think she's a wonderful artist and I love the way she's so rude to people,” the late Tony Wilson once said of Madonna.
evidence_packet.summary: “I think she's a wonderful artist and I love the way she's so rude to people,” the late Tony Wilson once said of Madonna. And he should know The Factory Records boss had first-hand experience with the pop superstar’s brusque manner after she performed at the Haçienda in 1984 for
evidence_packet.evidence_text: “I think she's a wonderful artist and I love the way she's so rude to people,” the late Tony Wilson once said of Madonna. And he should know The Factory Records boss had first-hand experience with the pop superstar’s brusque manner after she performed at the Haçienda in 1984 for the princely sum of £50 The bargain price gig was negotiated by television executive Malcolm Gerrie, who persuaded Madonna's record company to organise her appearance at the venue as part of a one-off, live Channel 4 broadcast of cult music show The Tube View 4 Images Madonna performing at The Hacienda, Manchester, on an episode of The Tube (Image: Channel 4/The Tube/YouTube screengrab) Free ticket-holders to the Haçienda showcase on January 27, 1984 were there to see the Factory Allstars - a band pulled together for the night by members of Durutti Column, A Certain Ratio, Quando Quango and soul singer Marcel King. So they were bemused when Madonna rocked up on Flanked by two Lycra-clad backing dancers, the then 25-year-old spun and gyrated as she sang Holiday. Her brother Christopher Ciccone - who was a backing dancer at the Haçienda gig - recounted their time in Manchester in his book, Life With My Sister

evidence_packet.lead: NHS Bullying and safety fears at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust as hundreds of staff report issues The concerns were shared in a report View 3 Images MFT runs hospitals across the city, employing more than 30,000 members of staff Comments News Declan Carey Local Democ
evidence_packet.summary: NHS Bullying and safety fears at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust as hundreds of staff report issues The concerns were shared in a report View 3 Images MFT runs hospitals across the city, employing more than 30,000 members of staff Comments News Declan Carey Local Democ
evidence_packet.evidence_text: NHS Bullying and safety fears at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust as hundreds of staff report issues The concerns were shared in a report View 3 Images MFT runs hospitals across the city, employing more than 30,000 members of staff Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 07:23, 05 Sep 2026 Updated 07:23, 05 Sep 2026 Hundreds of hospital workers in Manchester have reported experiences of safety fears as well as bullying and harassment at work, according to a report from the country’s largest NHS Workers at the Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) reported more than 380 incidents in total over the past year, up from 204 incidents in 2023-24. Staff concerns reported included ‘bullying behaviours by people in positions of authority’ and ‘harassment linked to pro Many reported experiencing issues with ‘unprofessional behaviour’ and ‘leadership approaches leaving colleagues feeling undervalued, anxious or unsafe at work’ They also raised concerns over intense workload pressures, such as staffing gaps and rota changes putting staff at risk of ‘burnout’ while working in Manchester’s healthcare facilities MFT runs hospitals across the city including North Manchester General Hospital, Manchester Royal Infirmary, and Trafford General, employing more than 30,000 members of staff in total

title: Blood, sweat, tears and Manchester United: The story of the Irish in Trafford

evidence_packet.title: Blood, sweat, tears and Manchester United: The story of the Irish in Trafford
evidence_packet.lead: Premium Blood, sweat, tears and Manchester United: The story of the Irish in Trafford An exhibition of Irish history and culture in the borough is being planned View 5 Images Navvies working on the Manchester Ship Canal which took six years to build Comments News Neal Keeling Chi
evidence_packet.summary: Premium Blood, sweat, tears and Manchester United: The story of the Irish in Trafford An exhibition of Irish history and culture in the borough is being planned View 5 Images Navvies working on the Manchester Ship Canal which took six years to build Comments News Neal Keeling Chi
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Premium Blood, sweat, tears and Manchester United: The story of the Irish in Trafford An exhibition of Irish history and culture in the borough is being planned View 5 Images Navvies working on the Manchester Ship Canal which took six years to build Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 07:12, 05 Sep 2026 It was a link forged with blood sweat and tears. It was later bolstered by Gaelic talent gracing the home of The Red Devils The Irish connection to the borough of Trafford is woven deep through the history of its industry and sporting legends In this corner of Greater Manchester, navvies toiled over six years to create the foundation of a magnificent feat of engineering - the Manchester Ship Canal. It opened for traffic from January 1, 1894. It cost more than £15m, equivalent today to £2.1bn Queen Victoria officially opened the canal on May 21, 1894 An estimated 17,000 workers grafted to make the 36 miles waterway from Salford to the Irish Sea. Workers came from Ireland - around 5,000 of them. The others came from Scotland, Wales, and South West England as well as the streets of Manchester and Salford

title: Police probe vile hoax TikTok knife threats as bag checks carried out at Salford school

evidence_packet.title: Police probe vile hoax TikTok knife threats as bag checks carried out at Salford school
evidence_packet.lead: Salford Police probe vile hoax TikTok knife threats as bag checks carried out at Salford school The Manchester Evening News understands there is no link between an knife attack in Walkden and a suspected hoax at Co-op Academy Walkden News Chris Slater Images seen by the Mancheste
evidence_packet.summary: Salford Police probe vile hoax TikTok knife threats as bag checks carried out at Salford school The Manchester Evening News understands there is no link between an knife attack in Walkden and a suspected hoax at Co-op Academy Walkden News Chris Slater Images seen by the Mancheste
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Police probe vile hoax TikTok knife threats as bag checks carried out at Salford school The Manchester Evening News understands there is no link between an knife attack in Walkden and a suspected hoax at Co-op Academy Walkden News Chris Slater Images seen by the Manchester Evening News were circulated on a social media platform, understood to be TikTok, on Thursday evening (September 3). One showed a hand holding a bladed weapon while another showed an image of armed police The picture of the knife carried the caption: 'Coop Walkden I'm After You Next.' After officers were called in over the disturbing content on the social media site, the MEN was contacted by a number of concerned parents of children at Co-op Academy Walkden in Salford The school acted quickly with security being stepped up including increased monitoring of access. Bag checks were also carried out, with nothing untoward being found following the purported threats, which are being treated as a hoax A second image shared on the social media platform featured a picture of an armed police officer and the words 'them tomorrow at coop academy walkden.'

As the public did not know about the enforcement, hundreds of bins were not collected prompting major backlash Those issues appear to have largely been resolved and last week, the council’s Liberal Democrat-administration announced major changes are coming with more collections to start later this year. From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025. It’s home to residents, currently up to 106 years of age. But also on the site is the Fernbees nursery, with youngsters aged from just six months, who regularly pop in for a tea break or lunch The two communities happily mix in an inter-generational model that has won praise from both its care users and the wider industry. Our Lifestyle Editor Dianne Bourne popped down for a visit and brought us this joyful despatch After the sing song in the main lounge, Dianne watched as the kids and older residents moved over to the bar area to tuck in to some tea, squash and cakes and have a chit chat. She describes the lovely image of June - a former Stockport mayor - playing games with the younger kids “The kids behave beautifully, they really do. I did wonder at first but they’re just lovely."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Mancunian Way ‘I hope one day there won’t be a need for Pride - we’re certainly not there yet’ As Manchester Pride ushers in a new dawn, a new Mancunian Way podcast looks at where it went wrong and what the future looks like for this vital event. “I hope one day - and I don't know whether it will be in my lifetime or not - there won't be a need for Pride because everyone will be equal,” says Steph Kay. “We're certainly not there yet.” It started with a few trestle tables and some games to raise money for AIDS sufferers. It transformed into a behemoth with international stars to rival the world’s biggest festivals View 4 Images All the thrills of the Manchester Gay Pub and Club Olympics in 1985 As a long-standing Gay Village businesswoman, Steph has seen Manchester Pride take many forms. The former manager of lesbian bar Vanilla has worked and partied throughout the event over decades. She was, at one time, a trustee of the event But Steph says the festival ‘snowballed’ after she left, with organisers deciding to hire bigger artists and venues. It was these decisions that culminated in the controversial choice to move Pride out of the Village entirely

evidence_packet.summary: Courts Stockport murderer who kidnapped girl off street and sexually attacked her in horror eight-hour ordeal jailed for life Paul Sharpe held his victim hostage for eight hours before they were found by police in a hotel car park News Stephen Topping A convicted murderer who kid
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Stockport murderer who kidnapped girl off street and sexually attacked her in horror eight-hour ordeal jailed for life Paul Sharpe held his victim hostage for eight hours before they were found by police in a hotel car park News Stephen Topping A convicted murderer who kidnapped a girl at knifepoint before sexually assaulting her has been jailed for life. Paul Sharpe held his 15-year-old victim hostage during a grim eight-hour ordeal, as he drove from one car park to another The 56-year-old put the girl in a headlock and bundled her into his car on Bradgate Road, in Altrincham , at around 7.30pm on May 18 - claiming that her father owed him money. He drove to a car park at Manchester Airport and tied up her ankles and wrists with a neck tie That night, he drove to different car parks in Greater Manchester and Cheshire, and plied the girl with alcohol while sexually assaulting her. At one point, former radio DJ Sharpe masturbated while touching the girl's feet, the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said He was finally caught by police in a hotel car park in Knutsford at around 3.40am on May 19. The girl had been reported as missing by her mother, while CCTV allowed officers to identify Sharpe's car, according to the CPS Greater Manchester Police says the girl had been studying at Sale Library on May 18 before beginning her journey home with friends at around 5:50pm. At 6:10pm, she contacted her parents to let them know she was on her way home

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Jury sworn in at trial of Stockport husband accused of drugging and raping wife with 12 co-defendants The husband, a man in his 60s from Stockport, denies 33 charges News Andrew Bardsley and Amy Walker Court reporter 12:37, 04 Sep 2026 View 4 I A jury has been sworn in at the trial of 12 men accused of sexual offences after a husband allegedly drugged and raped his wife over a number of years The husband, a man in his 60s from Stockport, denies 33 charges, including conspiracy to rape, conspiracy to commit assault by penetration, conspiracy to administer a substance with intent, rape and sexual assault. The charges relate to a 20 year period The Manchester Evening News and other media organisations are not naming the man in order to protect the anonymity of his alleged victim. The law entitles the alleged victim to anonymity for life The other 12 defendants deny the charges against them. They are Karl Lindsay, Daniel Rayner, Graham Brougham, Philip Wild, Mohammed Sabir, Jonathan Kirk, Sean Peers, Jordan Wallace, Alan Keelan, Richard Townsend, Robert Stewart and David Graves. All charges relate to the same sin A jury of 12 people, nine women and three men, were sworn in at Minshull Street Crown Court on Friday (September 4). They were sent away until Wednesday morning (September 9). Two alternative jurors, two women, were also selected

evidence_packet.evidence_text: M67 Police issue major update one month after human remains discovered next to M67 Officers have made a breakthrough News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 12:27, 04 Sep 2026 View Image Police and forensics officers on the M67 after the discovery of hum Police have issued a major investigation update a month after human remains were found next to the M67 motorway. Road workers made the tragic discovery near a bridge between junctions three at Hyde and four at Hattersley on Monday. August 3 The motorway remained closed eastbound the following day as officers and forensics investigators carried out enquiries. Greater Manchester Police later confirmed that the remains were believed to belong to a man aged between 20 and 28 He was thought to have been between 5ft 5ins and 5ft 9ins tall, and of medium build. In a further update issued today (September 4), GMP says it has since identified the person's next of kin Officers are continuing to establish the circumstances of how the man ended up where he did and what caused his death. Details on when the man may have died are yet to be confirmed The discovery was made by road workers during routine maintenance on the M67, in Tameside . A Home Office post-mortem later took place as officers tried to piece together the clues of what happened to the man. Enquiries remain ongoing

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Christie Hospital Lancashire dad determined to walk daughter down the aisle hails Manchester trial as 'better than a lottery win' Jason Walker is fighting on thanks to a new trial at The Christie Comments News Amy Walters and Stephen Topping Senio A dad with incurable cancer is fighting on to walk his daughter down the aisle - and hopes to 'be around for at least 'another 10 years'. Jason Walker was given a devastating diagnosis after experiencing persistent back pain and double vision At first, he thought they were simply signs of ageing, but the symptoms only worsened. Jason was diagnosed with stage three multiple myeloma, a type of blood cancer, which was terminal He went on to spend five years in remission but last November several lumps were found, with tests confirming he had relapsed. But after becoming the first patient to take part in a new trial at The Christie , the 57-year-old has big plans for the future “I need to get through this, as I’m giving her away,” the painting business owner, from Lancashire , said. “I want to be well enough to walk my beautiful daughter down the aisle “It’s every father’s dream to give their little girl away. And for her to be happy and settled with the man she loves. I can’t wait for that moment to see her in her wedding dress - it will be emotional

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

evidence_packet.summary: New Manchester research suggests tackling the factors behind suspensions could help prevent repeated exclusions and support vulnerable pupils School suspensions are associated with a complex combination of socioeconomic disadvantage, special educational needs, peer relationships
evidence_packet.evidence_text: New Manchester research suggests tackling the factors behind suspensions could help prevent repeated exclusions and support vulnerable pupils School suspensions are associated with a complex combination of socioeconomic disadvantage, special educational needs, peer relationships and pupils’ experiences of school, according to new research from The University of Manchester The study analysed survey responses from more than 19,000 secondary school pupils linked to administrative records across Hampshire & Isle of Wight, to examine a wide range of factors associated with whether pupils were suspended and how often suspensions occurred Researchers found pupils receiving special educational needs (SEN) support or with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) were more than twice as likely to be suspended than pupils without SEN, while those eligible for free school meals were also at increased risk The analysis also identified a number of factors associated with lower suspension risk, including pupils feeling that they belonged at school, being satisfied with their academic attainment, having positive relationships with school staff and having stronger emotion regulation sk By contrast, higher levels of peer pressure, experiences of bullying, and recent substance use were associated with an increased likelihood of suspension

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The family are Altrincham FC season ticket holders Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Lois (second right) with husband Ollie and kids Imogen and Jacob A local mum of two is fighting for her life in hospital after a liver transplant that almost killed her Lois Kinder, 44, was rushed to hospital in mid-July after becoming critically ill with acute liver failure. Within days she was placed in an induced coma and transferred to the specialist liver intensive care unit at Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham, one of only a handful of c On 22 July a donor liver became available, but during the operation she suffered three cardiac arrests after a blood clot blocked the main artery to her lungs, leaving her starved of oxygen for a prolonged period. Surgeons told her husband Ollie more than once that she was unlike Against the odds she pulled through. Six weeks on she is conscious and recognises her family, but the lack of oxygen caused significant brain damage to both sides of her brain. She cannot move, remains on a ventilator and dialysis, and is still in critical care “She’s conscious. She is recognising who we are,” Ollie said. “She’s saying the odd word, albeit very, very weak. She can’t move or anything like that at the moment. They’re hopeful of a form of recovery, but whether she will walk again remains unknown.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: PHM’s headline exhibition for 2026, On The Line: 100 years of strikes & solidarity (on show until 2 November 2026), is accompanied by an exciting programme of events exploring the exhibition’s themes and the stories represented in PHM’s nationally recognised collection Find out more about the exhibition and the full programme of events below You are invited to power up your imagination and build your own mini robot from a simple sheet of paper! Inspired by the Deceptioncon robot costume currently on display in On The Line , which once stood on the picket line in support of workers’ rights Explore strikes and solidarity and create textiles inspired by your discussions in this artist led workshop Join a guided tour of the On The Line exhibition, with lead curator Mark Wilson exploring the vibrant visual culture that has grown around strike action Explore a century of struggles and stories of strength drawing on the museum’s nationally significant collections. This free exhibition is part of the national commemorations, marking 100 years since the 1926 General Strike

evidence_packet.lead: An exhibition of Irish history and culture in the borough is being planned
evidence_packet.summary: An exhibition of Irish history and culture in the borough is being planned
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Premium Blood, sweat, tears and Manchester United: The story of the Irish in Trafford An exhibition of Irish history and culture in the borough is being planned View 5 Images Navvies working on the Manchester Ship Canal which took six years to build Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 07:12, 05 Sep 2026 It was a link forged with blood sweat and tears. It was later bolstered by Gaelic talent gracing the home of The Red Devils The Irish connection to the borough of Trafford is woven deep through the history of its industry and sporting legends In this corner of Greater Manchester, navvies toiled over six years to create the foundation of a magnificent feat of engineering - the Manchester Ship Canal. It opened for traffic from January 1, 1894. It cost more than £15m, equivalent today to £2.1bn Queen Victoria officially opened the canal on May 21, 1894 An estimated 17,000 workers grafted to make the 36 miles waterway from Salford to the Irish Sea. Workers came from Ireland - around 5,000 of them. The others came from Scotland, Wales, and South West England as well as the streets of Manchester and Salford

evidence_packet.evidence_text: 17 октября 2026 года в Brixton Jamm состоится концерт Наталки Карпы в Лондоне В Лондоне прозвучит украинская песня, и снова найдет своих людей, ведь на сцену выйдет Наталка Карпа — певица, чей голос уже более двух десятилетий остается голосом света и искренней любви к родной земле. Для многих украинцев за границей ее концерт станет не только художественным Наталья Карпа получила два высших образования, однако именно музыка стала делом ее жизни. От первых фестивалей и конкурсов до больших сцен Украины и мира, от песни “Калина”, открывшей ей путь к широкому признанию, до многочисленных сольных концертов и международных туров для укра Заслуженная артистка Украины, автор десятков популярных композиций, продюсер и общественный деятель в своем репертуаре легко сочетает лирическую нежность и праздничную энергию, а рядом с хорошо известными хитами непременно звучат новые композиции. Недаром поклонники после концерт В Лондоне прозвучат песни, сопровождавшие разные поколения украинцев, будут звучать слова, в которых живут любовь, вера и несокрушимость. Музыка преодолевает расстояния, находит дорогу к сердцу независимо от того, где человек живет сегодня, и оставляет после себя огонь жизни! evidence_packet.evidence_text: Say hello to Sister Moon, a beautiful new restaurant bringing a taste of Southeast Asia to Manchester city centre It’s the latest addition to Manchester’s Treehouse Hotel, which opened last year transforming a huge building at the end of Deansgate This is the final chapter of its new opening, and it might be our favourite one yet Sister Moon is the new project from acclaimed chef Sam Grainger who you’ll know from Madre, among others Sam is working alongside Luke Cowdrey and Justin Crawford (Electric Chair, Volta, Freight Island) at Sister Moon, a Southeast Asian BBQ concept inspired by his time cooking with a local family in Thailand All the dishes are cooked on open fire, including dishes like the fried pork skewers with banana ketchup and the grilled prawns with crispy chilli and garlic

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
